Model parameters and controlparameter ranges specific to individual calculations are given in the corresponding figure captions. A. Duffing dynamics and stroboscopic sampling The driven Duffing oscillator is written as the first-order system ẋ = v, v̇ = −γv − αx − βx3 + F cos(ωdt). (S1) Trajectories are obtained by direct numerical integration of Eq. (S1) with a fixed-step fourth-order Runge–Kutta scheme. We use ns = 200 integration steps per driving period for the calculations associated with Figs. 1, 2, and 6 of the main text, while the higher-resolution Feigenbaum analysis of Fig. 4 uses ns = 400 steps per period. For each value of the control parameter, an initial transient is discarded before any observable is evaluated. The stroboscopic trajectory is then constructed by sampling once per driving period, zn = [x(nTd), v(nTd)] , Td = 2π ωd . (S2) Periodic cycles, chaotic bands, and their cyclic permutation are identified from these post-transient stroboscopic states. Unless stated otherwise, initial conditions are those specified in the corresponding figure caption, since different attractors may coexist in parts of parameter space. Whenever coherent continuous-time Fourier components are required, we evaluate them directly on the posttransient trajectory rather than inferring them from the height of a discrete Fourier-transform bin.
